description:
LANDED d2a5f3510 on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-02. Cold review
(prototype mandate, approve-with-fixes, all six fixes folded) + adversarial
refutation (FIX-THEN-MERGE; its fix folded; its counterexample pinned).
Coordinator gate on the folded commit: see the PR section.

THE RULE, as built (callsite_dispatch.rs):
  unroutable(N) <=> exists W != N: stands_in_for(W, N) && !seats_before(N, W)
  stands_in_for(W, N) = same callee && surface_inside(N, W) && !surface_inside(W, N)
                        && test_inside(N, W)
  seats_before(x, y)  = covers(x, y) && (!covers(y, x) || strictly_inside(x, y))
one free function read by the seat and the drop; questions and observable
surfaces projected ONCE in routable_alternatives and threaded into
specificity_order; grouped_by_question is the one spelling of "one question =
one group"; the `groups` parameter of the drop and the seat's private copy of
its relation are gone.

WHAT IT CLOSED: the un-dropped-narrow-arm hazard (a split question group
re-arming a blind-escape seat under a blocked insertion). Escape census, base
-> head: settled 3 -> 3; arms:1 3 -> 3; arms:2 5 -> 3; arms:3 5 -> 3; arms:4
3 -> 3; arms:5 3 -> 3; arms:6 7 -> 5. Every entry that left was a
dispatch_list_head_separates narrow arm; the five that remain are fz-kdt.131
facet 3 (overlap without containment), incl. two enum_predicate_search pairs
only arms:6 reaches, out of this rule's reach because that [int] arm's
CALLABLE surface is strictly wider than its sibling's. The census gate now
drives arms:1..6 as well as settled, unordered pairs, per-setting constants.

MEASURED (base a3a9761d1 vs head, release binaries): canon movers exactly 4
(dispatch_list_head_separates, receive_map_pattern, receive_list_cons_pattern,
receive_interleaved_tuple_arity); behaviour 0 movers on interp and JIT over
597 fixtures, AOT identical on the 4; dispatch sites 51 -> 51, arm lines
126 -> 106; receive_* fixtures 8 Kernel.dbg/1 arms -> 2, define_function
46 -> 34 / 49 -> 37 / 49 -> 37, executables 25 -> 13 each (fz-kdt.140's
2^arity product: the MINTING is still 140's); dispatch_list_head_separates
arms 4 -> 2 (the callsite settles FOUR arms, not the trio the fixture header
claimed; header corrected), define_function 111 -> 111 because x32/x33 stay
reached by direct call edges; enum_map_family 827 -> 827, 00277 784 -> 784 --
the original premise of this ticket was refuted, nothing here recovers code
on those two.

GATES: three unit tests rewritten (red at base): the narrow twin the seat
would not put first is no destination; an arm whose head overlaps a wider one
is no destination beside it; the list-head trio drops the covered arm on all
six arrivals. Three boundary pins: 118's population in one question (map
axis), precision on a separating axis (int beside int|float both survive,
narrow first), and the shape_only-degraded narrow arm ([int|:ok] & not([:ok]))
that is NOT dropped -- the test-containment conjunct is load-bearing and not
implied by surface containment. Regression check: reintroducing the group-
local restriction turns exactly the three rewritten tests and the census gate
red.

RESIDUE, named and owned: the drop can DISSOLVE a question group (a dropped
arm sharing its question with a survivor un-pins that survivor and precision
seats it ahead of the arm that used to swallow its values). Pinned by
a_drop_that_dissolves_a_question_group_reseats_the_survivor_it_pinned; zero
corpus callsites carry the precondition; meaning-bearing only when the two
arms are different callees, which is the semantic layer's ambiguity ->
fz-kdt.176. Also recorded: a collapse to Direct removes the plan's fail node
across the whole arm set now (corpus impact 0 at 51 sites; fz-kdt.104's
inherited hazard). Stale doc corrected in passing: no fixture aborts natively
under any arm seed (28/28 exit 0).

COORDINATOR GATE (fresh, marker COORD-GATE-1788403091, HEAD d2a5f3510):
fmt clean; build 0 warnings; clippy -D warnings clean; lib 1590 passed / 0
failed / 5 ignored; fixture_matrix --test-threads=1 485 / 0 / 9 (known-red
set unchanged: enum_tier0, enumerable_protocol_dispatch, fz_f98_map_reduce).

comments.text: SAFETY DIMENSION added by the fz-kdt.107 step-3 refutation (2026-09-02, cc fz-kdt.131): losing fz-kdt.118's drop when a question group splits is not only +native code -- an un-dropped narrow list arm is a NEW BLIND-ESCAPE SEAT under legal arrivals base could never produce. Measured: under arms:3 the head-refined trio callsite's census reports 5 escapes where the settled order pins 3; the two extras are [int]-before-[int|:ok|:true] and [int]-before-[int|:ok] -- seatings impossible at base because 118 dropped both narrow arms (only two destinations settled). Zero behavior impact today (585x2-door + 30 seeds x JIT + 8 x AOT all clean), and the settled-order census is structurally blind to it (scope note added to the gate); fz-kdt.141's stress is the instrument that sees them. This ticket's cure (test-containment drop) closes the seats, not just the bytes.

title: A redundant arm survives only where the seat would put it ahead of its stand-in: the drop is the seating relation read the other way
